subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add explicit `first-progress` and `startup-failed` lifecycle phases for sub-agent startup, or solve startup silence using existing terminal outcome/session state semantics?
rationale: This is not just a line-level bug fix: it creates new core lifecycle semantics that downstream gateway, SDK, and subagent consumers must understand.

options.title: Adopt typed lifecycle phases
options.body: Add `first-progress` and `startup-failed` through active current-main runtime, registry, gateway, SDK, docs, and tests.

options.title: Stay within terminal outcomes
options.body: Improve aborted/error attribution and user-visible failure reporting without adding new lifecycle phase names.

options.title: Defer to sandbox proof first
options.body: Keep this blocked until the related sandboxed subagent startup issue supplies live proof for the exact failure mode.

recommendation.title: Adopt typed lifecycle phases
recommendation.body: Add `first-progress` and `startup-failed` through active current-main runtime, registry, gateway, SDK, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is on the active lifecycle and gateway/session projection surfaces that would need the contract decision.
